body: Split-adjusted ₹3.22 (Mar 2009) → ₹2,148 on 19 Nov 2026 ≈670x (ATH ₹2,270, Sep 2026). Twin engine: P/E 5.0 → 45.5 (9x) × implied EPS ~73x. Drawdowns: −84% (2008–09, before), −40% (2013), −57% (Jan 2018–Feb 2019). Early signal: a 'commodity' steel-tube maker with only 5–8% operating margin but ROCE 20–32%, high asset turns and branded distribution. In 2016–17 it installed India's first Direct Forming Technology (DFT) lines (Hosur, Raipur), making new hollow sections that replace angles and channels in construction. Reported structural-tube share ~40% by FY20. Working capital financed by dealers ('growth doesn't cost a rupee', smallcase). In 2013 the stock was at P/E ~4–5. Investors who tracked volumes and new-product share each quarter caught the 2014–2021 rerating. Not ended: FY26 PAT ₹1,203 cr (+59%), sales ₹23k cr, P/E ~45. 2018–19 −57% came from a steel-price slump and channel destocking, not a broken thesis. Lesson: low margins aren't the problem when asset turns are high and share is rising; screen on ROCE and volume growth, not OPM.

data.early_signals: ROCE >20% at 5% margin; DFT tech 2016-17; ~40% share
data.note: Prices: screener.in weekly closes, split/bonus-adjusted. P/E = trailing (TTM) from screener chart; 'implied EPS x' = price multiple / P/E multiple.

title: APL Apollo 2009–2026: low-margin steel tubes, ~670x via share gains
